title: The Arrows of Christ and the Rule of Virtue
english: If the person is the Father, he says: 'Since I alone am good' (Ps 44:2a), 'it is necessary that the one becoming the word of my own essence also be good.' But if the prophet is the one saying: 'Since a good man brings forth good from the good treasure of the heart' (Ps 44:2a), it is necessary that one having much good, having been fed with fornication foods, also brings forth a good word seeking it. For just as one having eaten an apple sends forth a scent of apple breathing, so one having eaten good things, having accustomed his soul to good things, brings forth a good word seeking it. Just as the quality of these foods is what becomes, so also regarding spiritual teaching, such things were sought and eaten.

Writing also certain instructions (Ps 44:2c). For just as the word of the gospel, being compared to a grain of cinnamon, if it should happen to be agriculture, becomes greater than human words of vegetables because of the temporary names given, so the word of God writes with his own pen and timely demonstrates these things, touching the thoughts and piercing the souls, apart from human writings.

Those hearing the words of Jesus, being full of grace (Ps 44:3bc), will say the upcoming text: 'He has poured out abundance' shows the grace; this agrees with 'I will pour out from my spirit upon all flesh' (Acts 2:17) and 'The love of God is poured out in our hearts' (Rom 5:5); for in these the abundance of the spirit and the wealth of the love from God is shown. Because of this poured-out grace, 'God has blessed you with your lips' (Ps 44:4), testifying of blessedness to you for all eternity.

Since regarding the testicle the things of generation are at work, and shameful desires grow around these, there is a need for the divisive word called a sword, in order that, having been made alive regarding the testicle, the unrestrained pleasures be cut away. The Savior, descending according to the human pattern, girds a sword around his testicle for the sake of self-sufficient purity, possessing beauty and loveliness because of the virtue coming forth in sinlessness; and what the symbol of the testicle of the aforementioned things is, let it be clear. For even Abraham, when sending the child for a bride, says his hand...

[...] upon my thigh, and I adjure you, the God of heaven. Perhaps, because of Him who is to become Savior through it, the Word who became flesh is able according to the flesh. The Word is understood and believed as a sword, while the flesh is a thigh from which the beginning of the flesh comes from there. But the Word, having escaped all weakness, is powerful, possessing the brightness, beauty, and splendor of divinity.

As for Psalm 44:5, the archer directs his best bow, wounding those who are thrown into divine arrows. It must also be read that he directs [them] to provide joy; and along with these, 'reign, O King, among the wounded' (Ps 44:6). The reason for your reigning is the perfection of virtue, not in practice alone but also in knowledge, because of truth, gentleness, and justice; for he says, 'reign, because it is necessary for the truth, gentleness, and justice to be known and established by those under your rule.' And 'your right hand shall guide you marvelously' (Ps 44:7). He who does all things according to God is marvelously guided by the right hand of good practice, using that path toward the Savior. And the Savior, performing paradoxical powers by his right hand, is marvelously guided.

As for Psalm 44:6ab, the words of the mighty Christ are like arrows that strike those who hear, so that they may judge the following of those toward Him. The apostles, being wounded by these arrows, having sent all things into the world, fell well to judge Him. And the peoples, who previously held a bad position, were struck by these arrows to be established in good, falling under Him; that is, they were made subject to Him and have become His.

As for Psalm 44:6c, the enemies of King Christ are all those who sin. If these spoken arrows do not exist in the hearts of these [sinners], they fall from the throne, prostrating themselves before the King. Perhaps the peoples who stand in the hearts of the King's enemies, being confirmed according to the will of their enmity, fell by the arrows under Christ, falling into the heart of His enemies.
As for Psalm 44:8, if these things are toward the only-begotten Son of God, the Son of God, having hated the life lived before His coming...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Change of Face and the Daughter of Tyre
english: Having loved iniquity, but having been granted righteousness through faith which comes from his presence by a paternal good pleasure, a man becomes and is anointed with the oil of gladness, that is, with the Holy Spirit. The garments of Christ breathe the scent of kingship and hierarchy through the death he undertook (for this is the fragrance imposed upon the buried dead), but also a continuous, unceasing scent of myrrh because of having something more than Christ's death for the salvation of others and the destruction of the devil, and of cassia because of his word being fiery; for this ointment is warming. The garments of Christ are those which are reasonably theologized about him. Since he did not take up along with the others that which is praised as being like a corpse, it is fitting that from his garments the aforementioned things breathe; with this, 'The fragrance of your myrrh is above all ointments' (Ps 44:9b) accords.

Kings are spoken of here as those co-reigning with Christ, while he himself is King reigning over them. Their daughters have become, according to teaching, educators of souls, or rather of the church; these daughters, in honor of the one being praised, have glorified the King, Christ. From ivory. But 'ivory' you say, [meaning] the high things of theology; for ivory, it happens, is a symbol of the Word, since the musical instruments and the teeth are vocal; and the great houses are heavy. Since they did not magnify their own word as the greatest of contemplations concerning God, many of the kings' daughters, from the aforementioned rich ivory, have glorified Christ.

The soul, having truly become a spouse to the true King Christ, is the church, and is named queen because it is the bride of the king, standing at his right hand to hold the right position, possessing its foundation in virtue and faith. And she also holds golden garments, having wrapped herself in Christ; and she is also draped and variegated, embracing the manifold wisdom of God. And one should not stumble because he himself is both bridegroom and clothed; for in one relation and another, and in one thought and another, these things exist, just as shepherd and lamb, and ten thousand other things are found in the Gospels.

A change of face appears to have happened (Ps 44:11); for God is the one calling the church from the Gentiles and naming her his daughter. He says: 'Having received my words, O daughter, listen and see their mind, having understood it for them; for what more will you desire to incline your will more fully toward them and to hear and long for them more effectively? And the forgetting of your kin will follow you, no longer desiring to restrain those same things and your fatherland; and the memory of your father who begot you according to the malice of the devil will also come upon you.'

Because of this I call you, daughter, says God to her, on account of the doing of the things commanded to you; since my son the king has desired the beauty existing in you according to the image and according to likeness having been made mine, and he, the king desiring your beauty, is not among your equals (Ps 44:12-14). For he is your Lord; for he is not an angel or an archangel or any other created being; for all worship him. Since it is not of God to be worshiped, be a god, the king desiring your beauty, who is also your Lord. Toward this also you undergo much change. For you, daughter of Tyre, because of which you had fear, have been made my daughter, so as to bring all the rich of the people as suppliants to your face. For all of the people from circumcision are becoming rich for you according to faith and are coming to you the truth of the gospel, beseeching your face to become a spouse to the king. For just as formerly those from the Gentiles, coming to the Godly service of Israel, were adhering to his face entreating him, so now those from the Jews, repenting, flee to the church of the Gentiles, deeming themselves worthy to be received by it. All the glory of the daughter of kings is Asbos. Asbos is interpreted as 'thoughts'. And the king of the thoughts being righteous is the Lord. The glory of the daughter of Tyre, which is being praised, is not other than that from the king of the thoughts. And it is to be understood that often in the Scriptures instead of the intelligible essence, gold is taken, as it will be timely shown. Since
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Christological Interpretation of the Psalms
english: Virtues are not merely found in the garments of the bride, nor is the discourse concerning the intelligible realities, especially that concerning the Trinity, adorned with golden embroideries; rather, it is made diverse through the varied and multifaceted teaching of Christ. Regarding Psalm 44:15a, since the word has an obscurity, we shall take its meaning from another. The discourse says that in the Vision of the Souls, it interprets the differences of the souls approaching Christ: 'There are queens and concubines and maidens without number; my dove is one, my perfect one' (Ps 44:15a). As it has been said concerning this: 'Her daughters have given her, and they shall bless her; queens and concubines shall praise her' (Ps 45:9), from which it is shown to one another that through the daughters they have been called maidens, concubines, and queens. It is made manifest from these words that the souls approaching Christ are such that some, having not yet the time for marriage, are maidens; but those coming to him after having been restored, some are noble and have ascended far above the world that became [existent] in six days. 'Sixty are queens,' [referring to] those having received the eight-day circumcision and possessing the spirit of the maturity of slavery. 'Eighty are concubines;' but the one surpassing them all according to the Spirit, having been perfected, to be a perfect dove of the Word, is the glorious Church, which has no nest, no wrinkle, or anything of that kind. The psalmist, in the verses preceding this, says that he hymns this Church, that she shall be brought to her bride with those [others] being embraced by him, the queens being the maidens who formerly did not have the time for cohabitation, but now, because they have been perfected, are being led into the bridal chamber, so that, having slept with the king, they might be taken up to become members of the one perfect bride, no longer being such as they happened to be when they were imperfect.

Regarding Psalm 44:15b, even if many are incorruptible, it is a custom to call souls virgins, but not all are brought to the king, but only those having become near and close by the disposition of the perfect bride. And also 'they shall be brought'; for those not having experience of the Word of the bride are not such as they are to go to him by themselves; but those handing the preliminary educations to them bring them to him; for they are not law and prophets.

Since almost everything of the psalm is said toward Christ, this verse says that although you have children according to the flesh from fathers, that is, those from circumcision, there have been born to you from the same race sons resembling the evangelical word. And these you also have established as rulers over all the earth, saying to them, 'Having gone, make disciples of all the nations' (Matt 28:19), they are his witnesses, having become the beginning of the king, even to the end of the earth.

Because of this, peoples will confess with thanksgiving (Ps 44:18), not for the sake of the second age, but even unto the age of ages. For we do not permit the confession concerning sins to be named now. For it never happens even unto the age of ages; only in this age is it possible to repent and to confess. But if they shall be remembered, according to another writing, instead of 'Those having been bequeathed to rule with you,' they shall be remembered by your name in all generations and generations, by extending your kingdom unto all the ages.

It is customary to call the things said unclearly 'hidden' because of a certain economy; for according to this also the wisdom of God is hidden in a mystery. Just so, 'The treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden' (Prov 2:6) have been said. And the end or purpose of these hidden things is not to let the unworthy find the knowledge of divine things, so that those having a desire for the attainment of divine knowledge, having given themselves to labors and exercises, might attain the purpose.

God is not the God of all, nor of those who have renounced all human refuge and power (Ps 45:2). For those fleeing toward God have all safety and power to partake of him, as the apostle says: 'I am able through him who strengthens me to do all things' (Phil 4:13). A help in the tribulations that find us intensely. The 'intensely' lies uncertainly; for the help is intensely in the tribulations that find us, or it is a help in the intensely finding tribulations.

Mountains being moved in the hearts of seas (Ps 45:3b), one should not consider the sensible parts of the earth being moved, but evil powers being moved into the souls disturbed by storms, a salty drink of wickedness and bitterness of character. Even the Savior toward the disciples...
